newsitem.title: INDIA: India allows foreign insurance liaison offices.
newsitem.headline: India allows foreign insurance liaison offices.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on Friday said it was allowing four foreign insurance companies to open liaison offices in India.

The RBI said it granted approval to Allianz Aktiengesellschaft Holding of Germany, Yasuda Fire & Marine Insurance Company of Japan, Zurich Insurance Company of Switzerland and Cigna International Corporation of the U.S.
"The liaison offices will act only as channel of communication between parties in India and their head offices," an RBI statement said.
"They are not permitted to undertake any insurance business in India," it said.
The insurance business in India is now a monopoly of state-run firms but the government has said it intends to open the sector to the private sector in the future as part of the economic reforms.
